title: Fact vocabulary, resolver feasibility and vitals survey
head: a4bebe24faffd52190c7e93bdc6d3fff91fa145c

reviews.classification: qualified governance and resolver/meter feasibility proposals
reviews.disposition: Retain the proposed registry fields, lifecycle, observer split, N1–N5 and C1–C8 with explicit implementation limits. MQ-A/B92 already settles L1 Q1/Q2: input.mass is fictional-mass (1000 per pack, 2000-reference dose), not inferred grams; procedure.process is the Village enumeration, with a separate frontier operation list. A {name:type} adapter cannot by itself enforce enum membership, units, revision locks, producer coverage or observer scope. S1’s claimed behavior neutrality therefore needs those actual checks; factRefs also changes the lock contract and is not a free no-format-change addition. N2’s asserted check:rules content corpus was only inference, not an existing checker capability. N5’s second-mechanism-fact requirement must not force dummy facts when designated identity is the real mechanism. Truth/knowledge means actual actor belief or understanding may affect a mechanism; labels alone do not confer authority. Keep unknown facts unknown and explanations projected. Registry, snapshot, migration and all-owner claims remain proposals, not new universal gates.
reviews.evidence: Complete original document read; selected rule_modules.js predicates/exports/target literals and simulation_contracts.js vital allow-lists inspected for the named current claims. Owner return sections 135–204 and 267–281 read, not whole owner.
reviews.reopen: A selected consumer needs current source, saved-lock/receipt compatibility and actual verification; no registry, new pool, migration or worktree is authorized by these proposals.

reviews.classification: qualified governance and resolver/meter feasibility proposals
reviews.disposition: Retain WR3/WR8/heredity examples, E1–E5, T1–T10 and R1–R8 as a source-level feasibility proposal. Current targeted rule_modules.js inspection still shows five default facts, injected fact types, one target, village.mix@2 literals and the original conflict message; this narrow source limitation remains, not a new failing runtime test. No module means no substitution policy only because the domain matcher supplies the refusal; absence of a module alone is not a general gate. Band specificity chooses an edge winner but must state the intended interval; facts support not/all/any predicates, not arbitrary numeric curves. Parameter suggestions are not capabilities until the body consumer grants them. Stateless resolver edits can still change saved consumer locks/receipts, so verify default equivalence before claiming no compatibility impact. AD51 allows designing from known world needs before a second implemented world; current AD41 does not require a new worktree. Keep actual target isolation, base and receiver checks when a slice is selected, without dispatching it here.

reviews.classification: qualified governance and resolver/meter feasibility proposals
reviews.disposition: Preserve M1-1–M1-3 as a dated reader survey, not an exhaustive present-day count or a two-edit effort guarantee. Current selected simulation_contracts.js still restricts vital effects and saved vital keys to health/stamina, but this does not prove all consumers, native sync, capacity/death rules or save behavior support a new key. Pool, accumulator, capacity and incapacitation semantics require their real owners. Energy-backed spirituality/strain meters are presentation over existing state and did not inherently add saved fields; this supersedes WDI55’s earlier assumed first-meter migration. The owner’s later M3 paragraph records code/tests and DOM values with explicit pixel/native persistence gaps; M1 alone does not close them. No fresh build/browser or meter acceptance is claimed.
